scope: Adult human functional hazard; animal experiments are supporting evidence, not transferred clinical tolerability.

tier_definitions.vital: Highest protection priority: plausible life-threatening failure, major irreversible neurological/sensory loss, or loss of indispensable regenerative support.
tier_definitions.protected: Persistent functional or structural injury is a major concern; compensation is incomplete or direct immune-depletion evidence is insufficient.
tier_definitions.manageable: A defined compartment has credible replacement, compensation or supportive-treatment precedent; acute inflammation and persistent recognition still require review.
tier_definitions.disposable: Narrow conditional allowance for loss of a specified compartment; does not imply painless, reversible or inflammation-free ablation.

interpretation: Tiers are ordinal policy judgments, not measured fatality probabilities or RNA cutoffs.
Regeneration after a finite insult does not establish recovery under persistent antigen recognition.
Recognized cells, inflammatory amplifiers and cells causing final organ failure can differ.
Bulk observations cannot receive a narrower cell-specific downgrade.
Reproductive/developmental membership is a separate axis, not a fifth severity tier.
Unknown identity, mixed cell labels and nonadult/nonhuman contexts cannot earn a cell-specific downgrade.

pardo2015.title: Parent stem cells can serve as niches for their daughter cells
pardo2015.finding: Approximately 79% ciliated-cell depletion did not accelerate replacement; basal and secretory populations persisted.
pardo2015.limitation: Large-airway homeostasis experiment, not human immune killing or a validated tolerability threshold.

dumm2019.title: Non-lytic clearance of influenza B virus from infected cells preserves epithelial barrier function
dumm2019.finding: Depletion of infection-surviving, predominantly ciliated-like cells worsened epithelial permeability and recovery.
dumm2019.limitation: Mixed survivor population in an infected lung; not selective depletion of healthy mature ciliated cells.

perl2011.title: Conditional Depletion of Airway Progenitor Cells Induces Peribronchiolar Fibrosis
perl2011.finding: Sustained club-compartment depletion caused persistent peribronchiolar fibrosis despite later epithelial regeneration.
perl2011.limitation: Promoter-defined compartment and toxin exposure do not quantify human receptor-specific risk.

guild2023.title: Evidence for lung barrier regeneration by differentiation prior to binucleated and stem cell division
guild2023.finding: AT2 differentiation rapidly compensated AT1 loss; repeated injury produced abnormal epithelial hyperplasia.
guild2023.limitation: Intact repair under finite experimental insults is not proof of tolerance to persistent T-cell attack.

garcia2016.title: Targeted Type 2 Alveolar Cell Depletion: A Dynamic Functional Model for Lung Injury Repair
garcia2016.finding: AT2 depletion produced recovery, fibrosis or lethal edema depending on severity and kinetics.
garcia2016.limitation: Drug toxicity and model kinetics prevent transfer of depletion percentages to clinical thresholds.

zhao2000.title: Alveolar epithelial cell chemokine expression triggered by antigen-specific cytolytic CD8+ T cell recognition
zhao2000.finding: Alveolar antigen recognition initiated inflammatory recruitment and progressive lethal lung injury.
zhao2000.limitation: Transgenic antigen and transferred T cells; not a human engineered-TCR clinical risk estimate.

haas2023.title: Two cases of severe pulmonary toxicity from highly active mesothelin-directed CAR T cells
haas2023.finding: Two severe pulmonary toxicities, one fatal, implicated benign pneumocyte expression in injured lung.
haas2023.limitation: AT1 versus AT2 initiation was not resolved; product, dose and pre-existing injury matter.

halbeisen2022.title: Lung function from school age to adulthood in primary ciliary dyskinesia
halbeisen2022.finding: Lung function declined on average in 486 patients, with heterogeneous trajectories despite treatment.
halbeisen2022.limitation: Inherited ciliary dysfunction is not epithelial ablation or an immune-toxicity model.

roy2014.title: Muc5b is required for airway defence
roy2014.finding: Muc5b deficiency impaired clearance and host defence, unlike Muc5ac deficiency.
roy2014.limitation: Mucin deletion is not goblet-cell killing; multiple secretory populations produce MUC5B.

tata2013.title: Dedifferentiation of committed epithelial cells into stem cells in vivo
tata2013.finding: Secretory cells restored basal stem cells after basal-cell depletion.
tata2013.limitation: Alternative repair depends on surviving populations and does not establish tolerance to repeated recognition.

clad2023.title: JAK-STAT activation contributes to cytotoxic T cell-mediated basal cell death in human chronic lung allograft dysfunction
clad2023.finding: Basal-cell MHC-I induction and cytotoxic T-cell killing were linked to airway-centered allograft injury.
clad2023.limitation: Alloreactivity affects multiple compartments and is not an isolated engineered-receptor trial.

bergmann2009.title: Evidence for cardiomyocyte renewal in humans
bergmann2009.finding: Carbon dating demonstrated limited adult cardiomyocyte renewal.
bergmann2009.limitation: Renewal is nonzero; a turnover estimate does not measure replacement during acute destructive injury.

linette2013.title: Cardiovascular toxicity and titin cross-reactivity of affinity-enhanced T cells in myeloma and melanoma
linette2013.finding: Titin cross-recognition by an engineered TCR caused fatal cardiac toxicity.
linette2013.limitation: Receptor-specific cross-reactivity; not evidence that every MAGEA3-directed receptor recognizes heart.

morgan2013.title: Cancer regression and neurologic toxicity following anti-MAGE-A3 TCR gene therapy
morgan2013.finding: Severe neurological injury was associated with a cross-reactive TCR and neural MAGEA12 expression.
morgan2013.limitation: Peptide and receptor specificity matter; rare RNA detection alone does not reproduce this evidence.

wharram2005.title: Podocyte depletion causes glomerulosclerosis
wharram2005.finding: Increasing podocyte depletion caused persistent proteinuria, sclerosis and renal dysfunction.
wharram2005.limitation: Model depletion thresholds are not human safety cutoffs.

grgic2012.title: Targeted proximal tubule injury triggers interstitial fibrosis and glomerulosclerosis
grgic2012.finding: Repeated tubular injury caused chronic atrophy, fibrosis and secondary glomerular injury.
grgic2012.limitation: Cre distribution and toxin sensitivity qualify compartment specificity; not clinical immune targeting.

raven2017.title: Cholangiocytes act as facultative liver stem cells during impaired hepatocyte regeneration
raven2017.finding: Biliary cells contributed hepatocytes when hepatocyte proliferation was impaired.
raven2017.limitation: Compensatory plasticity does not establish tolerance of combined biliary and hepatocyte destruction.

parkhurst2011.title: T cells targeting carcinoembryonic antigen can mediate regression of metastatic colorectal cancer but induce severe transient colitis
parkhurst2011.finding: CEA-directed TCR treatment caused severe transient colitis in all three treated patients.
parkhurst2011.limitation: Recovery in a small product-specific trial does not establish general controllability of persistent mucosal targeting.

tian2011.title: A reserve stem cell population in small intestine renders Lgr5-positive cells dispensable
tian2011.finding: Alternative progenitors maintained intestinal epithelium during Lgr5-cell depletion.
tian2011.limitation: An Lgr5-specific insult is narrower than destroying all crypt regenerative populations.

maude2018.title: Tisagenlecleucel in Children and Young Adults with B-Cell Lymphoblastic Leukemia
maude2018.finding: Responders developed B-cell aplasia; immunoglobulin replacement was commonly used.
maude2018.limitation: Manageability requires support; this does not generalize to all lymphocytes or marrow progenitors.

tran2013.title: Immune targeting of fibroblast activation protein triggers recognition of multipotent bone marrow stromal cells and cachexia
tran2013.finding: FAP-reactive T cells recognized marrow stromal cells and caused severe systemic toxicity.
tran2013.limitation: Target distribution and receptor properties matter; not all fibroblasts or all FAP products have equivalent effects.

roberts2013.title: Depletion of stromal cells expressing fibroblast activation protein-alpha from skeletal muscle and bone marrow results in cachexia and anemia
roberts2013.finding: Distributed FAP-positive stromal depletion disrupted muscle and hematopoietic support.
roberts2013.limitation: Distributed target-defined cells differ from a localized dermal fibroblast population.

wang2014.title: Targeting Fibroblast Activation Protein in Tumor Stroma with Chimeric Antigen Receptor T Cells Can Inhibit Tumor Growth and Augment Host Immunity Without Severe Toxicity
wang2014.finding: A different FAP CAR achieved antitumor effects without the severe toxicity of other models.
wang2014.limitation: Counterevidence emphasizes receptor/epitope and target-density dependence, not universal stromal safety.

sambasivan2011.title: Pax7-expressing satellite cells are indispensable for adult skeletal muscle regeneration
sambasivan2011.finding: Satellite-cell depletion prevented normal muscle regeneration after injury.
sambasivan2011.limitation: Localized experimental depletion does not estimate human systemic immune toxicity.

murphy2011.title: Satellite cells, connective tissue fibroblasts and their interactions are crucial for muscle regeneration
murphy2011.finding: Fibroblast depletion altered satellite-cell dynamics and impaired regenerated myofibers.
murphy2011.limitation: Niche-specific dependence cannot be generalized to all fibroblast populations.

stamatouli2018.title: Collateral Damage: Insulin-Dependent Diabetes Induced With Checkpoint Inhibitors
stamatouli2018.finding: Checkpoint treatment was associated with insulin deficiency and frequent ketoacidosis at presentation.
stamatouli2018.limitation: Checkpoint autoimmunity is not selective engineered-TCR beta-cell killing; insulin replacement is ongoing support.

iyer2018.title: Immune-Related Thyroiditis with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors
iyer2018.finding: Destructive thyroiditis often progressed to hypothyroidism requiring hormone replacement.
iyer2018.limitation: Controlling hormone deficiency does not establish control of acute inflammatory injury.

hypophysitis2021.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor related hypophysitis: diagnostic criteria and recovery patterns
hypophysitis2021.finding: Pituitary hormone deficits showed limited recovery, particularly the adrenal axis.
hypophysitis2021.limitation: Anatomical swelling, affected axes and hormone support distinguish patients; not a cell-specific ablation trial.

rama2010.title: Limbal Stem-Cell Therapy and Long-Term Corneal Regeneration
rama2010.finding: Limbal-cell grafts restored corneal epithelial maintenance after destructive injury.
rama2010.limitation: Successful transplantation does not make spontaneous limbal recovery reliable or treat retinal injury.

golub2012.title: Hair Cell Replacement in Adult Mouse Utricles after Targeted Ablation of Hair Cells with Diphtheria Toxin
golub2012.finding: Adult vestibular hair-cell loss was followed by limited replacement.
golub2012.limitation: Utricular findings do not establish restoration of human cochlear hearing.

shin2011.title: Hedgehog/Wnt feedback supports regenerative proliferation of epithelial stem cells in bladder
shin2011.finding: Urothelial and stromal signaling supported epithelial regeneration after injury.
shin2011.limitation: Repair after finite injury is not evidence that continuous urothelial killing is tolerable.

spalding2008.title: Dynamics of fat cell turnover in humans
spalding2008.finding: Adult adipocytes turn over while population size is regulated.
spalding2008.limitation: Turnover does not establish the metabolic tolerability of generalized adipocyte destruction.

johnson2009.title: Gene therapy with human and mouse T-cell receptors mediates cancer regression and targets normal tissues expressing cognate antigen
johnson2009.finding: Melanocyte-antigen TCR therapy injured skin, eye and ear compartments.
johnson2009.limitation: Cutaneous depigmentation cannot justify ocular or cochlear melanocyte depletion.

warner2019.title: Sicca Syndrome Associated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy
warner2019.finding: Checkpoint-associated sicca included persistent salivary hypofunction.
warner2019.limitation: Symptom improvement did not guarantee restoration of secretion; not selective receptor targeting.

kristinsson2014.title: Long-term risks after splenectomy among 8149 cancer-free American veterans
kristinsson2014.finding: Splenectomy was associated with lasting infection and thromboembolic risks.
kristinsson2014.limitation: Observational organ-removal evidence is not systemic immune-cell depletion.

kooshesh2023.title: Health Consequences of Thymus Removal in Adults
kooshesh2023.finding: Adult thymectomy was associated with adverse long-term health outcomes.
kooshesh2023.limitation: Observational association, potential confounding and adult context limit causal inference.

heinemeier2016.title: Radiocarbon dating reveals minimal collagen turnover in both healthy and osteoarthritic human cartilage
heinemeier2016.finding: Adult articular collagen showed very limited turnover.
heinemeier2016.limitation: Matrix turnover is not chondrocyte turnover or a direct immune-injury experiment.

braaten2020.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced inflammatory arthritis persists after immunotherapy cessation
braaten2020.finding: Inflammatory arthritis could persist after checkpoint treatment stopped.
braaten2020.limitation: Mixed joint tissues; not selective cartilage-cell ablation.

nhs_tonsillectomy.title: Making a decision about recurrent tonsillitis in children and adults
nhs_tonsillectomy.finding: Tonsil removal is an established treatment with recognized procedural risks.
nhs_tonsillectomy.limitation: Local removal is not systemic lymphocyte depletion.

nhs_appendix.title: Appendicitis
nhs_appendix.finding: Appendectomy permits survival without the appendix.
nhs_appendix.limitation: Removal does not establish tolerance of in-situ perforation or shared intestinal targeting.

niddk_gallbladder.title: Treatment for Gallstones
niddk_gallbladder.finding: Cholecystectomy is an established treatment for symptomatic gallstones.
niddk_gallbladder.limitation: Does not justify bile-duct or liver targeting, or uncontrolled in-situ inflammation.

niddk_adrenal.title: Definition and Facts of Adrenal Insufficiency and Addison's Disease
niddk_adrenal.finding: Adrenal insufficiency can cause crisis and requires hormone replacement.
niddk_adrenal.limitation: Replacement availability does not establish acute-injury control.

nci_lymph_nodes.title: Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy
nci_lymph_nodes.finding: Regional nodal surgery can cause lymphatic morbidity.
nci_lymph_nodes.limitation: Regional excision is narrower than distributed lymphatic injury.

sitc2021.title: SITC clinical practice guideline on immune checkpoint inhibitor-related adverse events
sitc2021.finding: Immune injuries span organ-specific acute and persistent consequences.
sitc2021.limitation: Checkpoint-toxicity management cannot validate engineered-cell killing for an untested compartment.

hpa_tissues.title: Human Protein Atlas tissue and cell-type definitions
hpa_tissues.finding: Defines tissue and cell annotations used for expression mapping.
hpa_tissues.limitation: Anatomy supports identity, not tolerability or receptor recognition.

openstax_female.title: Anatomy and Physiology: Female Reproductive System
openstax_female.finding: Defines female reproductive organs and physiological functions.
openstax_female.limitation: Reproductive membership is independent of clinical hazard.

openstax_male.title: Anatomy and Physiology: Male Reproductive System
openstax_male.finding: Defines male reproductive organs and physiological functions.
openstax_male.limitation: Reproductive membership is independent of clinical hazard.

purba2019.title: CDK4/6 inhibition mitigates stem cell damage in a novel model for taxane-induced alopecia
purba2019.finding: Hair-follicle stem-cell injury was investigated in an experimental chemotherapy model.
purba2019.limitation: Chemotherapy injury is not immune ablation; permanent alopecia remains possible.

collin2021.title: A single cell atlas of human cornea that defines its development, limbal progenitor cells and their interactions with the immune cells
collin2021.finding: Distinguishes corneal and limbal cell populations.
collin2021.limitation: Cell identity and expression alone do not measure toxicity.

wang2021_bcma.title: Humoral immune reconstitution after anti-BCMA CAR T-cell therapy in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma
wang2021_bcma.finding: Normal marrow plasma-cell aplasia and prolonged hypogammaglobulinemia followed BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy.
wang2021_bcma.limitation: Myeloma, prior therapies and conditioning affect immune recovery; this is not an isolated healthy-plasma-cell ablation trial.

assessments.label: Heart
assessments.acute_loss: Pump or conduction failure can be immediately fatal.
assessments.persistent_loss: Lost contractile reserve and scar can persist.
assessments.repair: Adult cardiomyocyte renewal is limited, not absent.
assessments.management: Mechanical support/transplant are not routine compensation for target-mediated injury.
assessments.rationale: Protect bulk heart because expression cannot exclude contractile or conduction cells.
assessments.evidence_scope: Human antigen-directed T-cell injury or depletion provides a clinical anchor; findings remain receptor/product-specific and may not resolve every subset in this rule.

assessments.label: Blood vessels and endothelium
assessments.acute_loss: Leak, thrombosis and disrupted perfusion can injure several organs.
assessments.persistent_loss: Vascular remodeling and ischemic injury can persist.
assessments.repair: Endothelial repair depends on injury extent and the vascular bed.
assessments.management: No general replacement for distributed vascular function.
assessments.rationale: A broad vascular label does not locate a safely expendable vessel population.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Brain and spinal cord
assessments.acute_loss: Circuit disruption can cause major neurological disability or death.
assessments.persistent_loss: Neuronal loss and disconnection may be irreversible.
assessments.repair: Repair varies by lineage; preservation of some progenitors does not restore complex circuits.
assessments.management: Rehabilitation is not replacement of lost circuits.
assessments.rationale: Small specialized populations can have high consequence; bulk dilution cannot establish safety.
assessments.evidence_scope: Human antigen-directed T-cell injury or depletion provides a clinical anchor; findings remain receptor/product-specific and may not resolve every subset in this rule.

assessments.label: Peripheral nerve
assessments.acute_loss: Motor, sensory and autonomic failure may be disabling or life-threatening.
assessments.persistent_loss: Denervation and failed reinnervation can persist.
assessments.repair: Axonal repair requires surviving neurons, Schwann cells and permissive paths.
assessments.management: Support does not guarantee functional restoration.
assessments.rationale: Potential regeneration is insufficient for a default downgrade of a mixed nerve sample.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Eye and retina
assessments.acute_loss: Injury can cause vision loss.
assessments.persistent_loss: Retinal or optic damage may be irreversible.
assessments.repair: Corneal epithelial repair and retinal neural replacement are different processes.
assessments.management: Local treatment or grafting applies only to selected compartments.
assessments.rationale: A bulk eye sample cannot establish restriction to replaceable surface epithelium.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Inner ear
assessments.acute_loss: Hearing and balance may be lost.
assessments.persistent_loss: Sensory deficits can persist despite suppression of inflammation.
assessments.repair: Limited vestibular replacement in mice does not establish human cochlear regeneration.
assessments.management: Assistive devices do not fully replace native sensory function.
assessments.rationale: Critical sensory disability is included in Vital even when injury is not lethal.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Lung and bronchus
assessments.acute_loss: Diffuse injury can cause edema and respiratory failure.
assessments.persistent_loss: Fibrosis and impaired clearance can persist.
assessments.repair: AT2 and airway progenitors can repair finite injury but may be targeted themselves.
assessments.management: Ventilation treats failure without proving recovery or stopping recognition.
assessments.rationale: Bulk lung includes alveolar, vascular and regenerative compartments; use explicit cell subsets for narrower calls.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Liver
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of detoxification and synthetic function can be life-threatening.
assessments.persistent_loss: Fibrosis, cholestasis and depleted regenerative reserve can persist.
assessments.repair: Hepatocytes regenerate; biliary compensation depends on surviving lineages.
assessments.management: Transplantation is not a general workaround for persistent antigen recognition.
assessments.rationale: High regenerative capacity does not make widespread or repeated hepatic injury manageable.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Kidney
assessments.acute_loss: Filtration, electrolyte and volume failure can be life-threatening.
assessments.persistent_loss: Podocyte depletion and repeated tubular injury can cause sclerosis and fibrosis.
assessments.repair: Tubules and podocytes have different repair capacity; both matter in bulk kidney.
assessments.management: Dialysis is substantial support and does not prevent all injury consequences.
assessments.rationale: Retain high protection for both irreversible glomerular loss and sustained tubular injury.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Pancreas
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammatory injury and endocrine failure can cause acute severe illness.
assessments.persistent_loss: Diabetes and digestive insufficiency can require lifelong support.
assessments.repair: Endocrine and exocrine populations differ; bulk does not establish isolated beta-cell exposure.
assessments.management: Insulin and enzymes replace selected outputs, not all acute organ injury.
assessments.rationale: A broad pancreas signal retains Vital; isolated cell populations are assessed separately.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Adrenal gland
assessments.acute_loss: Glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid failure can precipitate crisis.
assessments.persistent_loss: Deficits require continuing replacement and stress dosing.
assessments.repair: Reliable restoration after destructive immune injury is unestablished.
assessments.management: Replacement mitigates deficiency but requires sustained clinical management.
assessments.rationale: Bulk adrenal cannot exclude multiple axes or rapidly destabilizing cortical injury.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Pituitary gland
assessments.acute_loss: ACTH failure and disturbed water balance may be life-threatening.
assessments.persistent_loss: Several hormone deficits may persist.
assessments.repair: Clinical inflammatory injury shows incomplete hormonal recovery.
assessments.management: Multiple hormones and fluid balance may need ongoing support.
assessments.rationale: A mixed pituitary sample cannot establish exposure limited to a readily compensated axis.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Thyroid gland
assessments.acute_loss: Destructive thyroiditis can release hormone and cause symptomatic thyrotoxicosis.
assessments.persistent_loss: Hypothyroidism may be permanent.
assessments.repair: Functional recovery is variable; the rationale is replaceable output rather than guaranteed regeneration.
assessments.management: Thyroid hormone replacement is an established form of compensation.
assessments.rationale: Manageable is conditional on controlling acute injury and maintaining replacement; not Disposable.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Parathyroid gland
assessments.acute_loss: Calcium disturbance can affect neuromuscular and cardiac function.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent hormone deficiency can require complex supplementation.
assessments.repair: Reliable regeneration after extensive immune injury is unestablished.
assessments.management: Replacement of mineral balance is feasible but imperfect.
assessments.rationale: Persistent homeostatic consequences justify more protection than a simple removable-gland analogy.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Salivary glands
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation can impair oral intake and secretion.
assessments.persistent_loss: Severe dryness, dental injury and infection risk can persist.
assessments.repair: Clinical symptomatic recovery need not restore salivary flow.
assessments.management: Symptomatic management incompletely replaces gland function.
assessments.rationale: Local accessibility does not ensure recovery of secretory tissue.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Bone marrow
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of blood-cell production can cause infection, anemia and bleeding.
assessments.persistent_loss: Stem-cell or niche depletion can prevent recovery.
assessments.repair: Requires surviving progenitors and a functional stromal niche.
assessments.management: Transfusion and transplantation do not establish general target tolerability.
assessments.rationale: Marrow is a mixed regenerative organ; mature B-cell experience cannot be generalized to it.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Blood
assessments.acute_loss: Distributed cell depletion can compromise oxygen delivery, hemostasis or host defence.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent targeting can prevent hematopoietic replenishment.
assessments.repair: Renewal depends on spared marrow and antigen distribution during maturation.
assessments.management: Lineage-specific support exists but is not equivalent across cell types.
assessments.rationale: Bulk blood must not inherit a mature B-cell exception.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Lymph nodes
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation can disrupt immune organization and drainage.
assessments.persistent_loss: Lymphatic and stromal injury may cause lasting dysfunction.
assessments.repair: Removal of one node does not model depletion of all nodes or shared lineages.
assessments.management: No complete replacement for distributed nodal organization.
assessments.rationale: Distinguish circulating immune cells from resident lymphatic and stromal structure.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Spleen
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammatory or vascular injury can be severe.
assessments.persistent_loss: Functional asplenia increases long-term infection risk.
assessments.repair: Other immune organs compensate incompletely.
assessments.management: Vaccination and infection management reduce, but do not remove, consequences.
assessments.rationale: Surgical survival supports partial compensation, not a low-consequence or Disposable designation.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Thymus
assessments.acute_loss: Immediate effects vary with age and pre-existing immune reserve.
assessments.persistent_loss: Loss of T-cell renewal may have delayed consequences.
assessments.repair: Adult involution does not establish absence of continuing function.
assessments.management: No routine full replacement of thymic function.
assessments.rationale: Adult thymectomy associations argue for protection; pediatric risk requires separate review.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Tonsil
assessments.acute_loss: In-situ inflammation, swelling or bleeding can still be serious.
assessments.persistent_loss: Local organ loss is often compensated by other immune sites.
assessments.repair: Allowance rests on local removal tolerance, not regeneration.
assessments.management: Surgery is a local precedent, not evidence for systemic immune-lineage depletion.
assessments.rationale: The exception requires restriction to tonsillar tissue and excludes the same lymphocyte lineage elsewhere.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Small intestine
assessments.acute_loss: Diffuse barrier failure can cause sepsis and fluid loss.
assessments.persistent_loss: Extensive loss can compromise nutrient absorption and renewal.
assessments.repair: Crypt alternatives can compensate for selected insults; shared progenitor targeting changes the result.
assessments.management: Nutritional support does not guarantee control of destructive enteritis.
assessments.rationale: Renewal alone does not justify lowering a whole-organ small-intestine finding.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Colon and rectum
assessments.acute_loss: Colitis can cause severe diarrhea, bleeding or perforation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent targeting can cause chronic injury and impaired repair.
assessments.repair: Mature cells renew if regenerative compartments survive.
assessments.management: Clinical recovery after some TCR injuries is not universal rescue.
assessments.rationale: Bulk bowel does not establish restriction to mature replaceable epithelium.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Esophagus and stomach
assessments.acute_loss: Mucosal injury can impair intake, bleed or perforate.
assessments.persistent_loss: Stricture and gland loss may be persistent.
assessments.repair: Renewal requires surviving progenitors and control of inflammation.
assessments.management: Supportive therapy and local access do not guarantee recovery.
assessments.rationale: Mixed mucosa, glands and muscle merit protection even where some lining cells renew.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Oral and upper-airway mucosa
assessments.acute_loss: Injury can impair swallowing, intake or airway patency.
assessments.persistent_loss: Scarring, dryness and sensory deficits can persist.
assessments.repair: Surface renewal differs from gland, neural and muscle repair.
assessments.management: Local treatment is conditional on injury extent and persistence.
assessments.rationale: Bulk mucosal labels cannot exclude important underlying structures.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Appendix
assessments.acute_loss: In-situ inflammation may perforate or spread.
assessments.persistent_loss: Organ absence can be tolerated after controlled removal.
assessments.repair: Removal tolerance, not regeneration, underlies the exception.
assessments.management: Surgery is not equivalent to uncontrolled antigen-directed destruction.
assessments.rationale: Restriction must be to appendix, not a shared bowel or immune lineage.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Gallbladder
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation, obstruction or bile leakage can be serious.
assessments.persistent_loss: Loss of storage function is generally compensated after removal.
assessments.repair: Allowance rests on organ-removal experience.
assessments.management: Adjacent bile ducts and liver are not covered by the exception.
assessments.rationale: Local removability supports a narrow allowance rather than permission for generic biliary cells.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Bladder and ureter
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation and obstruction can compromise urinary drainage.
assessments.persistent_loss: Stricture, poor compliance and barrier dysfunction can persist.
assessments.repair: Urothelial regeneration depends on intact progenitor/stromal signaling.
assessments.management: Diversion or reconstruction is substantial intervention, not ordinary compensation.
assessments.rationale: Renewing urothelium does not make distributed or muscular injury low consequence.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Skin
assessments.acute_loss: Extensive epithelial loss threatens barrier, fluid balance and infection control.
assessments.persistent_loss: Scarring, chronic wounds and lost appendages can persist.
assessments.repair: Repair depends on viable epidermal and appendage progenitors and injury extent.
assessments.management: Local treatment applies to selected injuries; extensive loss needs systemic care.
assessments.rationale: Bulk skin is broader than cutaneous melanocytes or hair follicles and must retain barrier concern.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Cutaneous melanocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation may accompany pigment-cell killing.
assessments.persistent_loss: Depigmentation may persist.
assessments.repair: Return of pigment is not required for the conditional allowance.
assessments.management: Sun protection and skin surveillance may be required.
assessments.rationale: Cutaneous restriction is essential; eye and inner-ear pigment cells are excluded.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Hair follicles
assessments.acute_loss: Follicular inflammation can be painful and extensive.
assessments.persistent_loss: Alopecia can be permanent after stem-cell injury.
assessments.repair: Regrowth depends on the surviving follicular stem-cell niche.
assessments.management: Loss is generally compatible with systemic function, but can be consequential to the patient.
assessments.rationale: An explicit follicular sample can receive a narrow allowance; generic skin stem cells cannot.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Adipose tissue
assessments.acute_loss: Widespread inflammatory injury may disturb metabolism.
assessments.persistent_loss: Generalized fat loss can cause major metabolic dysfunction.
assessments.repair: Adult turnover exists but does not imply rapid restoration of widespread loss.
assessments.management: Compensation depends strongly on extent, depot and metabolic reserve.
assessments.rationale: Conditional lower priority for limited depot injury; pan-adipocyte targeting needs an explicit extent review.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Skeletal muscle
assessments.acute_loss: Respiratory weakness or extensive myonecrosis may be life-threatening.
assessments.persistent_loss: Weakness and fibrosis may persist if regenerative support is damaged.
assessments.repair: Satellite cells and supportive fibroblasts are required for effective repair.
assessments.management: Support and rehabilitation do not replace destroyed respiratory muscle.
assessments.rationale: A generic muscle label cannot exclude diaphragm or distributed injury.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Smooth muscle
assessments.acute_loss: Vascular or visceral contractile failure can threaten perfusion and organ function.
assessments.persistent_loss: Dysmotility or structural remodeling can persist.
assessments.repair: Repair is site dependent and not established from a generic label.
assessments.management: No single replacement applies to all smooth-muscle sites.
assessments.rationale: Unknown anatomical site retains high protection; local uterine membership remains a separate scope.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Cartilage
assessments.acute_loss: Location determines consequences, including airway support.
assessments.persistent_loss: Matrix damage and deformity may be persistent.
assessments.repair: Adult articular collagen turns over slowly; this is indirect evidence for cell-loss effects.
assessments.management: Symptom control does not restore structural integrity.
assessments.rationale: Articular evidence supports protection; unknown cartilage site does not justify assuming a harmless joint compartment.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Testis
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation can cause pain and endocrine disturbance.
assessments.persistent_loss: Fertility and androgen production can be permanently lost.
assessments.repair: Germline renewal requires surviving stem and supporting cells.
assessments.management: Hormone replacement cannot restore fertility.
assessments.rationale: Reproductive expression is a CTA association axis, not evidence that testicular injury is harmless.
assessments.evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Ovary
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation may disrupt ovarian function.
assessments.persistent_loss: Oocyte depletion can cause irreversible infertility and endocrine failure.
assessments.repair: Finite reserve differs from a renewable epithelial barrier.
assessments.management: Hormone replacement does not replace oocyte reserve.
assessments.rationale: Reproductive membership must not be read as a severity category.
assessments.evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Reproductive ducts and accessory organs
assessments.acute_loss: Injury can cause inflammation, obstruction and mucosal damage.
assessments.persistent_loss: Infertility, scarring and functional losses may be persistent.
assessments.repair: Repair differs between glands, ducts, muscle and mucosa.
assessments.management: Selected removal is possible but not a general model for distributed immune injury.
assessments.rationale: Keep hazard separate from the project reproductive permission; broad organs contain several important cell populations.
assessments.evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Mammary tissue
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation may be substantial, particularly during lactation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Loss can impair lactation and cause permanent structural changes.
assessments.repair: Epithelial plasticity depends on physiological state and surviving progenitors.
assessments.management: Systemic survival is compatible with gland loss; patient context remains important.
assessments.rationale: Conditional lower priority applies to nonlactating adult context; reproductive membership remains independent.
assessments.evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Mature airway ciliated cells
assessments.acute_loss: Loss impairs clearance; cytotoxic elimination also disrupts epithelial integrity.
assessments.persistent_loss: Infection and chronic airway damage can accumulate during sustained depletion.
assessments.repair: Spared progenitors permit renewal, but selective depletion did not trigger rapid replacement in mice.
assessments.management: Airway clearance and infection treatment do not fully replace ciliary function.
assessments.rationale: Lower immediate loss-of-function concern than alveolar failure is plausible; slow renewal and chronic consequences prevent an automatic Manageable allowance.
assessments.evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

assessments.label: Airway club cells
assessments.acute_loss: Secretory and airway progenitor function may be lost.
assessments.persistent_loss: Repeated depletion can exhaust repair and leave lasting peribronchiolar fibrosis.
assessments.repair: Club cells themselves provide regenerative capacity; surviving basal or alternative populations may compensate only conditionally.
assessments.management: Ventilation treats failure without proving recovery or stopping recognition.
assessments.rationale: Club cells cannot be treated as merely replaceable mature luminal cells; persistent loss directly threatens airway repair.
assessments.evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

assessments.label: Airway basal cells
assessments.acute_loss: Depletion removes a principal conducting-airway regenerative compartment; immediate effects depend on existing epithelial integrity.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent loss can impair re-epithelialization and contribute to airway fibrosis.
assessments.repair: Surviving secretory cells can dedifferentiate after finite basal-cell loss in mice; shared targeting can remove this alternative.
assessments.management: Respiratory support does not replace the regenerative pool or establish control of continuing recognition.
assessments.rationale: Protect principal airway progenitors while recording secretory-cell dedifferentiation as conditional counterevidence.
assessments.evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

assessments.label: Mature airway goblet cells
assessments.acute_loss: Isolated loss principally disrupts mucus defence rather than alveolar gas exchange.
assessments.persistent_loss: Loss of secretory defence may permit recurrent infection and chronic injury.
assessments.repair: Secretory-state plasticity is possible, but replacement cells may remain targets.
assessments.management: Airway clearance and infection treatment do not reproduce all mucus-defense functions.
assessments.rationale: Mucin knockout and altered differentiation are not cytotoxic ablation; sparse direct evidence supports a provisional Protected call.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Unresolved airway secretory cells
assessments.acute_loss: A broad secretory label may include both mature mucus-producing cells and regenerative club populations.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent targeting may compromise defense and renewal, depending on the actual cell mixture.
assessments.repair: Unknown secretory identity cannot establish spared club or alternative progenitors.
assessments.management: Support for mucus clearance does not compensate for loss of regeneration.
assessments.rationale: A broad secretory label may include club progenitors or essential gland populations and cannot inherit a mature-goblet downgrade.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Airway ionocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Selective loss could alter airway ion transport and surface-liquid homeostasis.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent transport disturbance could impair mucus handling; selective immune-depletion outcomes remain unresolved.
assessments.repair: Rarity is not evidence of dispensability, and regeneration after selective immune loss is unestablished.
assessments.management: Compensation by other transport-expressing cells is a question for testing, not an established replacement strategy.
assessments.rationale: Specialized ion transport supports airway physiology; direct cell-depletion tolerability evidence is insufficient for a lower default.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Alveolar type 1 cells
assessments.acute_loss: Extensive uncompensated loss can disrupt the gas-exchange epithelial barrier.
assessments.persistent_loss: Repeated injury can drive abnormal epithelial repair; barrier dysfunction depends on compensation.
assessments.repair: AT2 cells can rapidly flatten and differentiate after finite AT1 injury; persistent recognition may alter repair states.
assessments.management: Ventilation treats failure without proving recovery or stopping recognition.
assessments.rationale: Barrier function merits high protection; record rapid AT2 compensation rather than describing AT1 cells as irreplaceable.
assessments.evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

assessments.label: Alveolar type 2 cells
assessments.acute_loss: Loss threatens surfactant function and can initiate edema and respiratory failure.
assessments.persistent_loss: Depletion can impair alveolar repair and initiate fibrosis.
assessments.repair: Recovery depends on surviving AT2/alternative progenitors, injury kinetics and supporting tissue.
assessments.management: Ventilation supports gas exchange but does not restore the surfactant-producing regenerative compartment.
assessments.rationale: Surfactant output and alveolar renewal combine immediate and regenerative consequences; animal depletion and antigen-specific injury support major hazard.
assessments.evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

assessments.label: Unresolved alveolar epithelium
assessments.acute_loss: Diffuse injury can cause edema and respiratory failure.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent injury can compromise alveolar repair and produce fibrosis.
assessments.repair: A broad pneumocyte label does not establish whether AT2 repair is spared.
assessments.management: Ventilation treats failure without proving recovery or stopping recognition.
assessments.rationale: Unresolved pneumocyte labels must not acquire the repair assumptions of an isolated mature subtype.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Pulmonary endothelium
assessments.acute_loss: Vascular leak, edema and impaired perfusion can disrupt gas exchange.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent microvascular injury can impair alveolar function and tissue repair.
assessments.repair: Alveolar epithelial repair does not establish endothelial recovery; vascular-bed and injury-extent effects matter.
assessments.management: Respiratory support does not replace a functioning pulmonary microvascular barrier.
assessments.rationale: The alveolar-capillary interface can fail through direct recognition or secondary inflammatory vascular injury.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Cardiomyocytes and conduction cells
assessments.acute_loss: Pump or conduction failure can be immediately fatal.
assessments.persistent_loss: Lost contractile reserve and scar can persist.
assessments.repair: Adult cardiomyocyte renewal is limited, not absent.
assessments.management: Mechanical support/transplant are not routine compensation for target-mediated injury.
assessments.rationale: Limited adult renewal and direct receptor-specific cardiac toxicity support high protection; electrically specialized subsets are not discounted by rarity.
assessments.evidence_scope: Human antigen-directed T-cell injury or depletion provides a clinical anchor; findings remain receptor/product-specific and may not resolve every subset in this rule.

assessments.label: CNS neurons
assessments.acute_loss: Circuit disruption can cause major neurological disability or death.
assessments.persistent_loss: Neuronal loss and disconnection may be irreversible.
assessments.repair: Repair varies by lineage; preservation of some progenitors does not restore complex circuits.
assessments.management: Rehabilitation is not replacement of lost circuits.
assessments.rationale: Protect specialized neural circuits even where a small fraction of cells expresses the target.
assessments.evidence_scope: Human antigen-directed T-cell injury or depletion provides a clinical anchor; findings remain receptor/product-specific and may not resolve every subset in this rule.

assessments.label: Astrocytes and oligodendroglia
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of ion buffering, metabolic support or myelin can disrupt neural function.
assessments.persistent_loss: Demyelination, secondary axonal injury and disrupted homeostasis can persist.
assessments.repair: Repair differs among astrocytes and oligodendrocyte-lineage cells; surviving progenitors do not guarantee restoration under repeated attack.
assessments.management: Supportive care cannot replace distributed glial functions.
assessments.rationale: Distributed support, myelination and homeostatic roles can make non-neuronal loss disabling; neuron-to-glia equivalence is a mechanistic inference.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Ependymal cells
assessments.acute_loss: Injury may disturb CSF-facing epithelial and ciliary functions.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent ventricular-lining injury may alter CSF homeostasis; direct selective clinical evidence is limited.
assessments.repair: Airway ciliated-cell replacement is not evidence for adult ependymal repair.
assessments.management: Treating downstream CSF disturbances would not necessarily restore the lining.
assessments.rationale: CSF-facing homeostasis and ciliary function warrant protection; airway-cilia policy must not be transferred to CNS ependyma.
assessments.evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Schwann cells
assessments.acute_loss: Motor, sensory and autonomic failure may be disabling or life-threatening.
assessments.persistent_loss: Denervation and failed reinnervation can persist.
assessments.repair: Axonal repair requires surviving neurons, Schwann cells and permissive paths.
assessments.management: Support does not guarantee functional restoration.
assessments.rationale: Myelination and regeneration support are both at stake; peripheral repair depends on surviving axons and support cells.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Retinal neurons and photoreceptors
assessments.acute_loss: Injury can cause vision loss.
assessments.persistent_loss: Retinal or optic damage may be irreversible.
assessments.repair: Adult human retinal circuit replacement is not reliably achieved after destructive loss.
assessments.management: Vision aids do not restore native retinal circuits.
assessments.rationale: Loss can irreversibly affect visual processing; a whole-eye immune-toxicity precedent does not resolve individual retinal lineages.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Retinal pigment epithelium
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of retinal pigment epithelial support can compromise photoreceptor function.
assessments.persistent_loss: Secondary photoreceptor injury and visual loss may persist.
assessments.repair: Restoring an organized functional RPE layer after diffuse immune loss is unestablished.
assessments.management: Cutaneous depigmentation experience does not establish compensation for retinal support loss.
assessments.rationale: Retinal support differs fundamentally from cutaneous pigment function; retain high protection.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Limbal stem/progenitor cells
assessments.acute_loss: Injury can cause vision loss.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent epithelial defects, corneal opacity and loss of vision can follow injury; retinal loss is a separate compartment.
assessments.repair: Loss of limbal reserve can prevent sustained corneal resurfacing; transplantation is conditional rescue.
assessments.management: Local treatment or grafting applies only to selected compartments.
assessments.rationale: Protect the regenerative compartment needed to maintain a transparent corneal surface.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Mature corneal epithelial cells
assessments.acute_loss: Surface defects can cause pain, infection and impaired vision.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent epithelial defects and scarring can impair transparency.
assessments.repair: Surface renewal depends on spared limbal and basal regenerative populations.
assessments.management: Local support and selected grafts do not guarantee recovery during persistent recognition.
assessments.rationale: Surface replacement is possible with spared limbal reserve; ulceration and scarring remain important.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Corneal endothelium
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of endothelial fluid regulation can cause corneal edema and impaired vision.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent edema and secondary structural changes can impair transparency.
assessments.repair: Routine complete functional restoration after extensive adult human endothelial loss is not established.
assessments.management: Selected endothelial grafting requires a permissive environment; it does not establish tolerance of continuing immune attack.
assessments.rationale: Corneal transparency and fluid control are high-consequence sensory functions; vascular-endothelial analogies are inappropriate.
assessments.evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Inner-ear hair cells
assessments.acute_loss: Hearing and balance may be lost.
assessments.persistent_loss: Sensory deficits can persist despite suppression of inflammation.
assessments.repair: Limited vestibular replacement in mice does not establish human cochlear regeneration.
assessments.management: Assistive devices do not fully replace native sensory function.
assessments.rationale: Do not generalize limited mouse vestibular regeneration to recoverable human hearing.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Hepatocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of detoxification and synthetic function can be life-threatening.
assessments.persistent_loss: Fibrosis, cholestasis and depleted regenerative reserve can persist.
assessments.repair: Hepatocytes regenerate; biliary compensation depends on surviving lineages.
assessments.management: Transplantation is not a general workaround for persistent antigen recognition.
assessments.rationale: Finite-injury regeneration is substantial but depends on survivors; distributed persistent loss threatens metabolic and synthetic function.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Cholangiocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Bile-duct epithelial injury can impair bile flow and initiate cholestatic inflammation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Duct loss, cholestasis and fibrosis can become chronic.
assessments.repair: Biliary repair and facultative hepatocyte contribution require surviving responsive populations.
assessments.management: Drainage or transplantation is substantial intervention; suppressing inflammation need not restore lost ducts.
assessments.rationale: Biliary injury can cause chronic cholestasis and fibrosis; shared biliary/hepatocyte expression removes a potential repair route.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Podocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Filtration-barrier disruption can cause substantial proteinuria.
assessments.persistent_loss: Progressive glomerulosclerosis and loss of filtration can follow depletion.
assessments.repair: Podocyte replacement is limited; remaining cells can compensate only within model-dependent bounds.
assessments.management: Dialysis does not restore the glomerular barrier and is not a simple replacement of podocyte function.
assessments.rationale: Selective depletion directly supports progressive filtration-barrier failure and sclerosis.
assessments.evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

assessments.label: Renal tubular epithelium
assessments.acute_loss: Filtration, electrolyte and volume failure can be life-threatening.
assessments.persistent_loss: Podocyte depletion and repeated tubular injury can cause sclerosis and fibrosis.
assessments.repair: Tubules and podocytes have different repair capacity; both matter in bulk kidney.
assessments.management: Dialysis is substantial support and does not prevent all injury consequences.
assessments.rationale: Renewal after limited injury does not protect against extensive or repeated loss of transport and homeostasis.
