assessments.evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

assessments.label: Mesangial cells
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of glomerular support and regulatory functions could impair filtration architecture.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent glomerular remodeling is a concern; selective human immune-depletion outcomes are unresolved.
assessments.repair: Podocyte and tubular depletion studies are adjacent-compartment evidence, not direct mesangial regeneration measurements.
assessments.management: Whole-kidney support does not establish manageable selective mesangial loss.
assessments.rationale: Glomerular structural support warrants protection; direct selective immune-killing evidence is limited.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Pancreatic beta cells
assessments.acute_loss: Insulin deficiency can present with life-threatening ketoacidosis.
assessments.persistent_loss: Insulin dependence may be permanent.
assessments.repair: Reliable restoration after destructive immune injury is not established.
assessments.management: Insulin replacement permits survival but creates lifelong monitoring and treatment needs.
assessments.rationale: A cell-specific compensated endocrine deficit differs from whole-pancreas injury; Protected records the lasting burden and acute crisis risk.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Pancreatic alpha cells
assessments.acute_loss: Glucagon deficiency could impair metabolic counterregulation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent loss may impair defense against hypoglycemia, particularly with coexisting insulin deficiency.
assessments.repair: Reliable recovery under ongoing alpha-cell recognition has not been established.
assessments.management: Beta-cell insulin-replacement experience does not establish compensation for counterregulatory loss.
assessments.rationale: Counterregulatory hormone loss can disturb metabolic control; beta-cell replacement experience does not establish alpha-cell safety.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Pancreatic acinar cells
assessments.acute_loss: Acinar destruction can initiate pancreatic inflammation and enzyme-mediated injury.
assessments.persistent_loss: Exocrine insufficiency and fibrosis can impair digestion.
assessments.repair: Repair after finite injury depends on surviving cells and the ductal/stromal environment.
assessments.management: Pancreatic enzymes can replace selected digestive outputs; they do not treat every consequence of acute pancreatitis.
assessments.rationale: Enzyme replacement can compensate selected output loss; inflammatory pancreatic injury can remain severe.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Pancreatic ductal cells
assessments.acute_loss: Duct epithelial injury can disrupt flow and promote pancreatic inflammation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Obstruction, fibrosis and secondary exocrine injury may persist.
assessments.repair: Ductal repair requires an intact tissue environment; continued antigen recognition could injure replacements.
assessments.management: Enzyme replacement does not correct duct obstruction or establish control of destructive inflammation.
assessments.rationale: Duct injury and obstruction can propagate parenchymal inflammation; mature secretory-cell arguments do not establish ductal safety.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Thyroid follicular cells
assessments.acute_loss: Destructive thyroiditis can release hormone and cause symptomatic thyrotoxicosis.
assessments.persistent_loss: Hypothyroidism may be permanent.
assessments.repair: Functional recovery is variable; the rationale is replaceable output rather than guaranteed regeneration.
assessments.management: Thyroid hormone replacement is an established form of compensation.
assessments.rationale: Replacement of thyroid hormone supplies direct clinical compensation precedent, conditional on acute-injury control.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Thyroid parafollicular cells
assessments.acute_loss: Selective calcitonin-cell loss differs from destructive injury to thyroid hormone-producing follicles.
assessments.persistent_loss: The endocrine consequence is loss of calcitonin secretion; selective immune-killing outcomes are poorly characterized.
assessments.repair: This call does not depend on proven C-cell regeneration.
assessments.management: Thyroidectomy provides indirect whole-organ survival precedent, but levothyroxine replaces follicular output, not calcitonin.
assessments.rationale: A restricted calcitonin-producing population has a different role from parathyroid calcium control; selective immune-killing evidence remains limited.
assessments.evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Adrenal cortical cells
assessments.acute_loss: Glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid failure can precipitate crisis.
assessments.persistent_loss: Deficits require continuing replacement and stress dosing.
assessments.repair: Reliable restoration after destructive immune injury is unestablished.
assessments.management: Replacement mitigates deficiency but requires sustained clinical management.
assessments.rationale: Hormone replacement exists, but rapid or persistent broad cortical injury can precipitate adrenal crisis.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Adrenal chromaffin cells
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammatory injury could disturb catecholamine release and cardiovascular responses.
assessments.persistent_loss: Medullary endocrine loss differs from adrenal cortical insufficiency.
assessments.repair: Reliable chromaffin-cell recovery under persistent immune recognition is unestablished.
assessments.management: Cortisol and mineralocorticoid replacement do not replace medullary function; extra-adrenal sympathetic compensation is an inference.
assessments.rationale: Catecholamine release and autonomic physiology require review; cortical replacement logic does not directly apply.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Pituitary corticotrophs
assessments.acute_loss: ACTH deficiency can cause secondary adrenal insufficiency and crisis.
assessments.persistent_loss: ACTH-axis deficits may require continuing glucocorticoid replacement.
assessments.repair: Clinical hypophysitis shows limited recovery of the adrenal axis; this does not resolve selective corticotroph killing.
assessments.management: Glucocorticoid replacement and stress dosing require ongoing management.
assessments.rationale: ACTH-axis failure can be acute and persistent; clinical hormone-deficit recovery is limited.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Other identified anterior pituitary endocrine cells
assessments.acute_loss: The consequence depends on the recognized hormone-producing subset and local inflammation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Loss of selected axes can cause lasting endocrine and reproductive dysfunction.
assessments.repair: Clinical recovery varies by hormone axis; mixed pituitary injury does not establish subset-specific regeneration.
assessments.management: Selected hormonal deficits can be supported, but replacement and monitoring differ by axis.
assessments.rationale: Restricted axes can be supported, but enduring endocrine loss is consequential; mixed pituitary labels retain Vital.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Salivary acinar cells
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation can impair oral intake and secretion.
assessments.persistent_loss: Severe dryness, dental injury and infection risk can persist.
assessments.repair: Clinical symptomatic recovery need not restore salivary flow.
assessments.management: Symptomatic management incompletely replaces gland function.
assessments.rationale: Persistent loss of salivary output is clinically documented even when inflammatory symptoms improve.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Salivary ductal cells
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation can impair oral intake and secretion.
assessments.persistent_loss: Severe dryness, dental injury and infection risk can persist.
assessments.repair: Clinical symptomatic recovery need not restore salivary flow.
assessments.management: Symptomatic management incompletely replaces gland function.
assessments.rationale: Drainage, secretion modification and repair may be impaired; local gland accessibility is not proof of reversibility.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Intestinal stem and undifferentiated crypt cells
assessments.acute_loss: Diffuse barrier failure can cause sepsis and fluid loss.
assessments.persistent_loss: Extensive loss can compromise nutrient absorption and renewal.
assessments.repair: Crypt alternatives can compensate for selected insults; shared progenitor targeting changes the result.
assessments.management: Nutritional support does not guarantee control of destructive enteritis.
assessments.rationale: Broad progenitor depletion threatens barrier renewal; selective Lgr5 ablation shows reserve, not tolerance of all regenerative-cell loss.
assessments.evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

assessments.label: Paneth cells
assessments.acute_loss: Loss can impair antimicrobial secretion and interactions with the crypt niche.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent loss may compromise host defense and regenerative support.
assessments.repair: Other niche cells can contribute support; selective Lgr5 depletion is not direct evidence for Paneth-cell tolerability.
assessments.management: Clinical control of colitis does not establish replacement of Paneth functions.
assessments.rationale: Antimicrobial and niche support functions differ from mature absorptive-cell loss; not a generic renewing-mucosa exception.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Mature intestinal absorptive cells
assessments.acute_loss: Diffuse barrier failure can cause sepsis and fluid loss.
assessments.persistent_loss: Extensive loss can compromise nutrient absorption and renewal.
assessments.repair: Crypt alternatives can compensate for selected insults; shared progenitor targeting changes the result.
assessments.management: Nutritional support does not guarantee control of destructive enteritis.
assessments.rationale: Regenerative reserve supports replacement after finite injury, while extensive persistent loss threatens absorption and barrier function.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Intestinal goblet cells
assessments.acute_loss: Colitis can cause severe diarrhea, bleeding or perforation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent targeting can cause chronic injury and impaired repair.
assessments.repair: Mature cells renew if regenerative compartments survive.
assessments.management: Clinical recovery after some TCR injuries is not universal rescue.
assessments.rationale: Mucus defence and epithelial interactions warrant protection; airway goblet and mucin experiments cannot establish gut-cell tolerability.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Enteroendocrine cells
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of distributed gut hormone signals could disrupt metabolic and digestive regulation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Deficits may affect motility, nutrient sensing and endocrine signaling.
assessments.repair: Replacement from crypt progenitors depends on survival and lack of repeated recognition.
assessments.management: No general replacement regimen establishes control of broad enteroendocrine-cell loss.
assessments.rationale: Distributed hormonal control cannot be inferred expendable from rarity; receptor-specific injury evidence is limited.
assessments.evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Unresolved bowel glandular epithelium
assessments.acute_loss: Colitis can cause severe diarrhea, bleeding or perforation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent targeting can cause chronic injury and impaired repair.
assessments.repair: Mature cells renew if regenerative compartments survive.
assessments.management: Clinical recovery after some TCR injuries is not universal rescue.
assessments.rationale: A broad glandular label does not establish mature-cell restriction or preserved crypt progenitors.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Basal epidermal keratinocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Extensive epithelial loss threatens barrier, fluid balance and infection control.
assessments.persistent_loss: Scarring, chronic wounds and lost appendages can persist.
assessments.repair: Repair depends on viable epidermal and appendage progenitors and injury extent.
assessments.management: Local treatment applies to selected injuries; extensive loss needs systemic care.
assessments.rationale: The regenerative epidermal compartment requires protection even when mature keratinocytes can be replaced.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Mature epidermal keratinocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Extensive epithelial loss threatens barrier, fluid balance and infection control.
assessments.persistent_loss: Scarring, chronic wounds and lost appendages can persist.
assessments.repair: Repair depends on viable epidermal and appendage progenitors and injury extent.
assessments.management: Local treatment applies to selected injuries; extensive loss needs systemic care.
assessments.rationale: Conditional lower priority requires mature-cell restriction and spared regenerative reserve; broad keratinocyte labels stay Protected.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Cutaneous melanocytes identified by cell label
assessments.acute_loss: Localized pigment-cell injury can cause inflammation and depigmentation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Depigmentation may persist; ocular and inner-ear melanocytes are outside this exception.
assessments.repair: Recovery depends on surviving pigment-cell and follicular reservoirs.
assessments.management: The allowance accepts a localized pigmentation deficit; it does not establish inflammatory control.
assessments.rationale: Local skin pigment-cell loss has a specific clinical precedent; this rule is anatomically restricted.
assessments.evidence_scope: Human antigen-directed T-cell injury or depletion provides a clinical anchor; findings remain receptor/product-specific and may not resolve every subset in this rule.

assessments.label: Hair-follicle cells identified by cell label
assessments.acute_loss: Follicular injury can cause inflammation and hair loss.
assessments.persistent_loss: Alopecia can be persistent when follicular regenerative cells are lost.
assessments.repair: Mature shaft-cell loss and stem-cell destruction differ in reversibility.
assessments.management: Hair loss can be accepted in a defined context; generic epidermal loss is not included.
assessments.rationale: Narrow follicular loss can be tolerated; permanent alopecia is possible and generic epidermal stem cells are excluded.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Sweat and sebaceous gland cells
assessments.acute_loss: Secretory loss can impair lubrication or sweating; extensive sweat-gland loss can impair heat control.
assessments.persistent_loss: Distributed gland loss may cause persistent dryness and thermoregulatory impairment.
assessments.repair: Regeneration and surviving reserve vary by appendage and injury extent.
assessments.management: Local skin care does not replace distributed thermoregulatory function.
assessments.rationale: Distributed gland loss has barrier and thermoregulatory consequences; hair-follicle permission cannot be extended to every appendage.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Dermal fibroblasts
assessments.acute_loss: Disruption of matrix and wound-support functions can impair tissue integrity.
assessments.persistent_loss: Poor wound repair and altered matrix organization may persist.
assessments.repair: Replacement requires viable stromal and epithelial interactions.
assessments.management: Local wound management does not establish tolerance of distributed fibroblast killing.
assessments.rationale: Matrix and repair support warrant explicit review; fibroblast identity alone does not establish dispensability.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Skeletal-muscle satellite cells
assessments.acute_loss: An isolated finite loss may spare existing fibers initially while depleting regenerative reserve.
assessments.persistent_loss: Subsequent or concurrent muscle injury can fail to regenerate and produce lasting weakness/fibrosis.
assessments.repair: Selective Pax7-compartment ablation directly impairs regeneration in experimental muscle injury.
assessments.management: Rehabilitation cannot restore an eliminated regenerative compartment; widespread consequences are a mechanistic inference.
assessments.rationale: Selective ablation demonstrates indispensable regenerative capacity in the tested model.
assessments.evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

assessments.label: Muscle fibroblasts and fibro-adipogenic support
assessments.acute_loss: Niche disruption can alter myogenic-cell dynamics during injury.
assessments.persistent_loss: Abnormal repair and matrix remodeling can persist.
assessments.repair: Experimental fibroblast depletion impairs regeneration; dependence is niche-specific.
assessments.management: Supportive care does not restore the cell interactions required for normal repair.
assessments.rationale: Repair depends on niche interactions; renewing stroma is not automatically low consequence.
assessments.evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

assessments.label: Articular chondrocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Location determines consequences, including airway support.
assessments.persistent_loss: Matrix damage and deformity may be persistent.
assessments.repair: Adult articular collagen turns over slowly; this is indirect evidence for cell-loss effects.
assessments.management: Symptom control does not restore structural integrity.
assessments.rationale: Matrix maintenance and lasting structural damage justify protection; anatomical site remains important.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Mature umbrella urothelial cells
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation and obstruction can compromise urinary drainage.
assessments.persistent_loss: Stricture, poor compliance and barrier dysfunction can persist.
assessments.repair: Urothelial regeneration depends on intact progenitor/stromal signaling.
assessments.management: Diversion or reconstruction is substantial intervention, not ordinary compensation.
assessments.rationale: Finite-injury regeneration is established, but barrier dysfunction and persistent targeting remain consequential.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Basal urothelial cells
assessments.acute_loss: Inflammation and obstruction can compromise urinary drainage.
assessments.persistent_loss: Stricture, poor compliance and barrier dysfunction can persist.
assessments.repair: Urothelial regeneration depends on intact progenitor/stromal signaling.
assessments.management: Diversion or reconstruction is substantial intervention, not ordinary compensation.
assessments.rationale: Protect regenerative and intermediate populations; continuous recognition can defeat surface renewal.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Mature B lymphocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Depletion reduces humoral defence and may accompany systemic inflammatory toxicity.
assessments.persistent_loss: Aplasia and hypogammaglobulinemia may persist.
assessments.repair: Renewal requires spared progenitors and cessation or evasion of recognition.
assessments.management: Immunoglobulin replacement and infection management have direct clinical precedent.
assessments.rationale: The exception is lineage specific and does not extend to HSCs, all marrow or all immune cells.
assessments.evidence_scope: Human antigen-directed T-cell injury or depletion provides a clinical anchor; findings remain receptor/product-specific and may not resolve every subset in this rule.

assessments.label: T lymphocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Distributed loss can impair cellular immune defense and immune regulation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent depletion can sustain susceptibility to infection and dysregulated immunity.
assessments.repair: Restoration depends on spared progenitors, thymic/peripheral reserve and antigen expression in replacements.
assessments.management: Antimicrobial support does not replace the range of T-cell functions.
assessments.rationale: Distributed cellular immunity cannot be assigned the mature B-cell compensation precedent.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells
assessments.acute_loss: Depletion can compromise phagocytosis, antigen presentation and tissue-specific maintenance.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent loss can impair defense and repair; tissue-resident subsets differ in replenishment.
assessments.repair: Blood-derived replenishment cannot be assumed equivalent to restoration of every resident macrophage population.
assessments.management: Antimicrobial and supportive treatment cannot fully substitute for distributed myeloid function.
assessments.rationale: Host defence and tissue-resident support vary by lineage and site; broad myeloid labels do not justify a low tier.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Granulocytes and NK cells
assessments.acute_loss: Loss can impair antimicrobial or cytotoxic innate defense; consequences differ by subset.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent depletion may sustain infection susceptibility.
assessments.repair: Marrow reserve can replenish some short-lived subsets if progenitors and replacements are spared.
assessments.management: Growth factors and antimicrobials have context-specific roles, not universal replacement of innate defense.
assessments.rationale: Regeneration may be rapid if progenitors survive, but ongoing depletion can impair host defence; lineage and extent require review.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of blood-cell production can cause infection, anemia and bleeding.
assessments.persistent_loss: Stem-cell or niche depletion can prevent recovery.
assessments.repair: Requires surviving progenitors and a functional stromal niche.
assessments.management: Transfusion and transplantation do not establish general target tolerability.
assessments.rationale: Distributed blood-cell renewal depends on surviving progenitors and niche support.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Marrow stromal niche cells
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of blood-cell production can cause infection, anemia and bleeding.
assessments.persistent_loss: Stem-cell or niche depletion can prevent recovery.
assessments.repair: Requires surviving progenitors and a functional stromal niche.
assessments.management: Transfusion and transplantation do not establish general target tolerability.
assessments.rationale: Targeted niche-cell injury can compromise hematopoiesis; stromal identity is not a safe exemption.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Erythroid cells
assessments.acute_loss: Extensive loss can reduce oxygen-carrying capacity and cause severe anemia.
assessments.persistent_loss: Repeated targeting of precursors or mature cells can prevent durable correction.
assessments.repair: Erythropoiesis requires spared progenitors, marrow support and nonrecognized replacement cells.
assessments.management: Transfusion is substantial repeated support and may be ineffective if donor cells share the target.
assessments.rationale: Oxygen transport and ongoing erythropoiesis are critical; mature erythrocytes differ in receptor accessibility from nucleated precursors.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Megakaryocytes and platelets
assessments.acute_loss: Platelet loss can cause serious bleeding and impaired hemostasis.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent megakaryocyte or platelet targeting can sustain thrombocytopenia.
assessments.repair: Platelet recovery requires spared megakaryopoiesis and survival of new platelets.
assessments.management: Transfusions may be short-lived if replacement platelets remain targets.
assessments.rationale: Persistent loss can undermine hemostasis; anucleate platelets and marrow precursors require distinct recognition evidence.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Other anatomically located fibroblasts
assessments.acute_loss: Distributed stromal injury can disrupt tissue support and repair.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent matrix, regenerative-niche or metabolic effects depend on anatomical distribution.
assessments.repair: Turnover does not demonstrate successful replacement during ongoing immune attack.
assessments.management: FAP-model outcomes differ by receptor and distribution; no general compensation precedent covers all fibroblasts.
assessments.rationale: Protect matrix and regenerative support until a site-specific exception is justified; FAP studies demonstrate target-dependent systemic liabilities.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Other vascular endothelial cells
assessments.acute_loss: Leak, thrombosis and disrupted perfusion can injure several organs.
assessments.persistent_loss: Vascular remodeling and ischemic injury can persist.
assessments.repair: Endothelial repair depends on injury extent and the vascular bed.
assessments.management: No general replacement for distributed vascular function.
assessments.rationale: Distributed vascular barrier and perfusion functions remain high priority across organs.
assessments.evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

assessments.label: Adipocytes
assessments.acute_loss: Widespread inflammatory injury may disturb metabolism.
assessments.persistent_loss: Generalized fat loss can cause major metabolic dysfunction.
assessments.repair: Adult turnover exists but does not imply rapid restoration of widespread loss.
assessments.management: Compensation depends strongly on extent, depot and metabolic reserve.
assessments.rationale: Retain conditional depot-level compensation; widespread adipocyte recognition requires a separate metabolic extent assessment.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Unresolved mature immune-cell mixtures
assessments.acute_loss: Loss of a mature immune-cell mixture can compromise host defense and regulation.
assessments.persistent_loss: Persistent depletion may impair antimicrobial and adaptive responses.
assessments.repair: Composition and surviving hematopoietic progenitors determine replacement.
assessments.management: A B-cell-specific replacement precedent does not establish compensation for an unresolved leukocyte mixture.
assessments.rationale: A mature leukocyte mixture does not establish B-cell restriction; preserve the broader concern for loss of cellular defense.
assessments.recognition_evidence: Mixed immune identity requires lineage resolution; no receptor-specific recognition is inferred.
assessments.evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

assessments.label: Plasma cells and plasmablasts
assessments.acute_loss: Loss reduces antibody secretion; consequences depend on residual antibodies and prior immune reserve.
assessments.persistent_loss: Prolonged plasma-cell aplasia can produce lasting deficits across immunoglobulin classes.
assessments.repair: Recovery requires surviving B-cell precursors, differentiation and cessation or evasion of recognition.
assessments.management: Immunoglobulin replacement provides partial support and does not reproduce all mucosal antibody functions.
assessments.rationale: Direct BCMA clinical evidence demonstrates lasting humoral deficiency. Protect this antibody-secreting compartment separately from mature circulating B cells.
assessments.evidence_scope: Human cell-therapy depletion provides a clinical anchor; disease, prior treatment and conditioning complicate attribution.
